title: How do we change grams into kilograms?
description: Weights in grams are written in kilograms by moving the point three places left, and two weights are changed back into grams. Keeko's doubt is that sixty-eight grams is zero point six eight kilograms.
teaching_notes: One idea: a gram is one thousandth of a kilogram, so the point moves three places. Watch for students who move the point only two places and skip the zero that holds the tenths place.

source: Fill in the blanks (g to kg): 465 g, 68 g, 1560 g, 704 g, and the grams in 0.56 kg and in 2.5 kg.
video_script.why: The child has changed millimetres into centimetres and centimetres into metres and now changes weights.
video_script.substitution: One gram is one thousandth of a kilogram, so the point moves three places when the unit changes.
video_script.anchor: a kilogram weight cut into one thousand grams
video_script.wrong_move: moves the point only two places, as for centimetres and metres
video_script.payoff_line: Grams to kilograms moves the point three places left

final_answer.spoken: zero point four six five, zero point zero six eight, one point five six and zero point seven zero four kilograms; five hundred sixty grams; two thousand five hundred grams

maths_rules: 68 g = 0.068 kg, with a zero in the tenths place
the slip: 0.68 kg is 680 g, not 68 g
video_script.design: The kilogram weight stays on the stage cut into one thousand grams; each weight slides to its place in the working band and the point moves three places. Keeko's doubt moves the point only twice.

narration: <bookmark mark='scene'/>This is a question from your book about changing grams into kilograms.
<bookmark mark='list'/>Weights such as four hundred sixty-five grams and sixty-eight grams are to be written in kilograms.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Two weights go the other way, from kilograms to grams.

beats.on_screen: the weights stay on the board; Keeko sits beside them as the child
narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

marks.kilo: the kilogram weight is cut into one thousand grams

narration: <bookmark mark='kilo'/>A kilogram has one thousand grams, so one gram is one thousandth of a kilogram.
<bookmark mark='thou'/>That is zero point zero zero one kilograms.

beats.on_screen: Given: 465 g, 68 g, 1560 g, 704 g, 0.56 kg and 2.5 kg
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, four hundred sixty-five, sixty-eight, one thousand five hundred sixty and seven hundred four grams.
Also zero point five six kilograms and two point five kilograms.

beats.on_screen: To find: the first four weights in kg, and the last two in g
narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to write the first four weights in kilograms, and the last two in grams.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: 1 g = 1/1000 kg, so the point moves 3 places left; 465 g = 0.465 kg

marks.move: an arrow shows the point moving three places left

narration: <bookmark mark='one'/>Step one, one gram is one thousandth of a kilogram.
<bookmark mark='move'/>The point then moves three places to the left.
<bookmark mark='c465'/>Four hundred sixty-five grams is zero point four six five kilograms.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: 68 g = 0.068 kg, with a zero in the tenths place

marks.zero: 68 moves three places and a zero fills the tenths place

narration: <bookmark mark='zero'/>Step two, sixty-eight grams needs a zero in the tenths place.
<bookmark mark='c68'/>It is zero point zero six eight kilograms.

marks.drop: the last zero is struck out to give 1.56 kg

narration: <bookmark mark='c1560'/>Step three, one thousand five hundred sixty grams is one point five six zero kilograms.
<bookmark mark='drop'/>The last zero can be dropped, so it is one point five six kilograms.
<bookmark mark='c704'/>Seven hundred four grams is zero point seven zero four kilograms.

marks.back: an arrow shows the other way

narration: <bookmark mark='back'/>Step four, go the other way by multiplying by one thousand.
<bookmark mark='k56'/>Zero point five six kilograms is five hundred sixty grams.
<bookmark mark='k25'/>Two point five kilograms is two thousand five hundred grams.

marks.l1: the first two weights are marked
marks.l2: the next two weights are marked
marks.l3: the last two weights are marked

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Grams to kilograms moves the point three places left.
<bookmark mark='l1'/>The first two are zero point four six five and zero point zero six eight kilograms.
<bookmark mark='l2'/>The next two are one point five six and zero point seven zero four kilograms.
<bookmark mark='l3'/>Going back, they are five hundred sixty grams and two thousand five hundred grams.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the kilogram weight
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: 68 g = 0.68 kg appears and is struck out; the weight shows 68 of the 1000 grams; 0.068 kg is written

marks.fix: 0.68 is struck out and 68 of the 1000 parts are shaded
marks.zero: a zero is placed in the tenths place

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks sixty-eight grams is zero point six eight kilograms, because the point moves two places.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>But a kilogram is one thousand grams, so the point moves three places.
<bookmark mark='zero'/>That leaves the tenths place empty, so it needs a zero. Sixty-eight grams is zero point zero six eight kilograms.
